title: The Apes and the Two Travellers
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: Two men were travelling together, one of whom never spoke the truth, whereas the other never told a lie: and they came in the course of their travels to the land of Apes.

The King of the Apes, hearing of their arrival, ordered them to be brought before him; and by way of impressing them with his magnificence, he received them sitting on a throne, while the Apes, his subjects, were ranged in long rows on either side of him.

When the Travellers came into his presence he asked them what they thought of him as a King. The lying Traveller said, "Sire, every one must see that you are a most noble and mighty monarch." "And what do you think of my subjects?" continued the King. "They," said the Traveller, "are in every way worthy of their royal master." The Ape was so delighted with his answer that he gave him a very handsome present.

The other Traveller thought that if his companion was rewarded so splendidly for telling a lie, he himself would certainly receive a still greater reward for telling the truth; so, when the Ape turned to him and said, "And what, sir, is your opinion?" he replied, "I think you are a very fine Ape, and all your subjects are fine Apes too." The King of the Apes was so enraged at his reply that he ordered him to be taken away and clawed to death.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how are the two Travellers different from each other?
options: One was rich, while the other was poor
One knew the land of Apes well, while the other had never visited
One never spoke the truth, while the other never told a lie
One traveled by foot, while the other rode a horse

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the King of the Apes receive the Travellers?
options: Sitting on a throne, with his subjects ranged in long rows
Standing at the entrance to greet them personally
Lying beneath a tree, uninterested in ceremony
Hidden behind a curtain to observe them first

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the lying Traveller say about the King?
options: That he is the wisest king in all the land
That he should rule over other kingdoms too
That his throne is the finest ever built
That he is a most noble and mighty monarch

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the lying Traveller say about the King's subjects?
options: That they should be given more respect by outsiders
That they are in every way worthy of their royal master
That they resemble their king in wisdom and courage
That they are the finest subjects in the entire world

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the King reward the lying Traveller?
options: He appoints him as an adviser
He invites him to stay in the palace
He gives him a very handsome present
He grants him safe passage through the land

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the honest Traveller say when asked his opinion?
options: That the King is a very fine Ape, and his subjects are fine Apes too
That the King should treat his subjects more kindly
That he has never seen a stranger kingdom in his travels
That he prefers not to answer such a question

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the King order done to the honest Traveller?
options: To be exiled from the land forever
To be given a smaller reward than the first Traveller
To be locked away until he apologized
To be taken away and clawed to death

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the honest Traveller expect an even better reward than his companion?
options: He believes the King specifically prefers criticism to praise
He assumes that telling the truth will be valued even more than the earlier flattering lie
He has been told in advance what answer the King wants
He plans to share his reward with his companion afterward

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the King react so differently to the two similar-sounding answers?
options: The first Traveller spoke more clearly than the second
The King had already decided to punish someone before either answer
The first answer flatters his vanity, while the second bluntly states what he actually is
The second Traveller repeated exactly what the first had said

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Truth is not always welcomed, especially by those who prefer flattering illusions about themselves
Kings are always fair judges of what they are told
Lying is always punished more severely than honesty
Travellers should avoid speaking to rulers about their own nature

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the King want to impress the Travellers with?
options: His wealth of gold
His army's strength
His knowledge of foreign lands
His magnificence

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what question does the King ask both Travellers?
options: How long they intended to stay
What they thought of him as a King
Where they had traveled from
Whether they wished to become his subjects

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what word does the lying Traveller use to address the King?
options: "Traveller"
"Stranger"
"Sire"
"Friend"

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what miscalculation does the honest Traveller make about the King's character?
options: He assumes the King values truth over flattering praise, which turns out to be false
He assumes the King cannot understand plain language
He assumes the King will reward both Travellers equally regardless
He assumes the King already knows he is an Ape

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the King's throne and rows of subjects suggest about how he wants to be seen?
options: As an approachable and humble leader
As someone uninterested in ceremony
As a king who prefers privacy over display
As a grand and impressive ruler deserving of praise

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "enraged" mean in "The King of the Apes was so enraged at his reply"?
options: Made very curious
Made extremely angry
Made deeply sad
Made pleasantly surprised

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: Both Travellers are rewarded equally for their honesty
The King forgives the honest Traveller after hearing his explanation
A flattering lie is rewarded richly while an honest truth leads to punishment
Both Travellers are punished for insulting the King
